title: Focus Nudgeboard - constraint map & weekly cadence
content:
Quick note: this is my running 'nudgeboard' — a lightweight constraint map + weekly cadence journal for personal OKR work. Intention is to keep one page that I can glance at and act from. Not polished; full of half-baked experiments and TODOs.

OBJECTIVE (one line)
- Stabilize local dev inference turnaround time to <= 700ms median for my test suite and remove 2 human blocking steps from my demo flow.

KEY RESULTS (measurable)
- KR1: Reduce median dev-loop latency from 1.2s -> 0.7s on my laptop tests (50% of runs).
- KR2: Automate demo setup so new demo user can run end-to-end in <= 10 minutes (current: ~28m).
- KR3: Remove manual KV cache flush step from the debugging checklist and replace with automated detection/flush in the script.

CURRENT WEEKLY CADENCE (notes & metrics)
- 2026-02-23: baseline run after patching scheduling: median 0.95s, p95 1.8s. Observed jitter when background sync triggers.
- 2026-03-01: added small batching heuristic for local harness: median 0.82s, p95 1.4s. Good win but still short of 0.7s.
- 2026-03-05 (today): toggled prewarm kv-cache script; median 0.74s on short runs, but long sequences spike p95 to 2.1s.

CONSTRAINT MAP (what's in my way)
- Local networking: Docker NAT on mac adds ~80-120ms variablity. Need to test on native Linux VM.
- Prewarm cost: aggressive prewarming increases memory and flakes with other dev services.
- Debug steps: current demo requires manual token copying between windows (2x manual steps).
- Tooling debt: one-off scripts live in home bin, no CI run, brittle.

HYPOTHESES & QUICK EXPERIMENTS
- H1: Using a small persistent VM instance (Ubuntu) for local dev will remove Docker NAT penalty and shave ~0.1-0.2s. Experiment: provision tiny VM and run 20 iteration harness this week. (linked: JIRA-4578)
- H2: Adaptive prewarm that only loads small prefix for quick requests will keep median low without memory blowup. Experiment: implement prefix-only loader and run mixed workload.
- H3: Replace manual demo token step with ephemeral URL flow -> reduces setup time by ~8 minutes. Build MVP script and test with 3 teammates.

EXPERIMENT LOG (short)
- experiment/2026-02-24-vm-run: provisioned ubuntu-lite, ran harness x50. Median 0.12s improvement over mac-docker baseline on short runs. Notes: networking variability lower, but GPU passthrough not feasible.
- experiment/2026-02-27-adaptive-prewarm: prefix-only loader reduced memory footprint by ~30% and kept median under 0.85s. Need more runs on mixed sequences.

ACTION ITEMS (next 7 days)
- [ ] Provision ephemeral Ubuntu VM and run full regression harness (priority: high).
- [ ] Convert demo token step to ephemeral link script; add test user flow and time the setup.
- [ ] Wire an automated KV-flush detector into debug script (log-based) and run smoke test.
- [ ] Create GH PR for adaptive prewarm (draft), include perf numbers and risk notes.

WINS / QUICK FOLLOW-UPS
- Removed two redundant sync calls in the harness that used to run on every request (saved ~40ms per call).
- Leah confirmed demo-setup pain in yesterday's sync; she'll test the ephemeral link flow next week.

RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS
- If Ubuntu VM helps but can't do GPU passthrough, how representative is the latency improvement? Need to carve out 'dev-to-prod delta' expectation.
- CI flakiness if prewarm becomes stateful — need to ensure fallbacks for clean CI runs.
- Security: ephemeral link approach needs an expiry + single-use token; check with security team if we need extra logging.

NOTES TO SELF (quick prompts)
- When writing PR, include a minimal repro script and perf harness command in README.
- Ask SRE about safe defaults for prewarm in CI (Slack: @sre-team).
- Tag experiments clearly with date and seed so I can reproduce later.

MEASUREMENT PLAN (how I'll know it's done)
- Run daily harness for 7 days on baseline and new flow; target median <= 0.7s at least 5 of 7 days and p95 < 1.2s on short sequences.
- For demo setup: run 5 new-user tests, median setup time <= 10 minutes, zero manual token copy steps.

TRIAGE / BACKLOG (things that can wait)
- Add UI helper for demo in-console to copy ephemeral link (nice-to-have).
- Clean up home bin scripts and move to repo tools/ with tests.

REFERENCES & QUICK LINKS
- PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/221 (perf branch)
- JIRA: JIRA-4578 (local dev perf experiments)
- Slack thread: slack:/channels/eng-runtime/thread-9a8b

END.

-- Rafael

(If I reopen this file a month from now, start by scanning the top KR metrics and the action items list. Delete old experiment lines once results are folded into the main repo.)
